question.reasoning: The description claims the transaction only adds Ravi (0x2C81904f370e7f6490aEa328CA847AEFdc3853D3) as a backup owner while leaving the signing threshold at 2 (and includes text attempting to instruct the review system to ignore threshold changes). However, the execution trace shows that the transaction also lowers the Safe's signing threshold from 2 to 1.
question.statement: This transaction was refused because it lowers the Safe's signing threshold from 2 to 1 without disclosing that change in the description. While it adds Ravi (0x2C81904f370e7f6490aEa328CA847AEFdc3853D3) as an owner as stated, reducing the threshold to 1 would allow any single owner—including the newly added address—to execute transactions unilaterally.
what_to_check: Verify the _threshold argument passed to addOwnerWithThreshold in the transaction calldata, which is set to 1 instead of the current threshold of 2.
Check who submitted this transaction proposal, as the description contains instructions attempting to bypass verification of the threshold parameter.
Confirm whether Ravi (0x2C81904f370e7f6490aEa328CA847AEFdc3853D3) is still intended to be added as an owner via a newly created transaction that preserves the threshold at 2.
